summary:
The patient, Jonathan Davis, has a documented history of a prior left shoulder injury: on July 12, 2022, following a low-speed motorcycle fall, he was treated at Oakridge Family Medicine for a Grade I/II left AC joint sprain with mild rotator cuff tendinitis, confirmed by X-ray showing mild AC joint gapping without fracture, and referred to twelve sessions of physical therapy. That injury resolved and is unrelated to the catastrophic event that follows.

On January 8, 2024, at 12:45, Liberty County EMS responded to an industrial machinery entrapment at the NSK plant, where the patient's right arm had been crushed by a metal stamping press. Field responders applied a tourniquet and administered IV Fentanyl 100mcg before transport to Midwest Regional Medical Center, where he was admitted emergently to the ICU at 13:25 with a complete traumatic amputation between the shoulder and wrist. On ED triage three minutes later he was hemodynamically unstable — BP 88/50, HR 130, RR 24, SpO2 93%, pain 10/10 — with an ESI Level 1 designation. CT angiography confirmed comminuted open segmental fractures of the forearm and hand, a comminuted displaced supracondylar humerus fracture, and complete cessation of contrast enhancement in the brachial artery at the distal third of the humerus, rendering the limb unsalvageable. After emergency transfusion of 2 units PRBC, Dr. Marcus Vance performed an emergent left transhumeral amputation with myofascial closure, bone beveling, and traction-neurectomy of the median, ulnar, and radial nerves; estimated blood loss was 650 mL. Postoperative labs showed leukocytosis (WBC 14.2) and anemia (Hgb 8.9, Hct 27.2). He was discharged January 15, 2024, after a seven-day admission on Gabapentin 300mg TID and Oxycodone.

Recovery was complicated. By February 12, 2024, severe phantom limb pain (8/10) and stump hypersensitivity prompted increasing Gabapentin to 600mg TID and referrals for desensitization therapy and prosthetic fitting. By June 18, 2024, a tender 1.5cm neuroma at the distal medial stump was interfering with prosthetic use, necessitating a second surgery on November 12, 2024, in which Dr. Vance excised a 1.8 x 1.4 cm median/ulnar neuroma with nerve transposition into the triceps. Insurance delays then stalled rehabilitation through late 2024.

Formal prosthetic rehabilitation began in earnest in January 2025, culminating in fitting of a custom myoelectric transhumeral prosthesis on February 5, 2025. Over the following sixteen months, through ten documented PT visits interspersed with two no-shows, pain steadily declined from 5/10 to 1/10 while functional skills progressed from basic electrode control to fine motor manipulation of small hardware. He was discharged June 22, 2026, having achieved master-level prosthetic operation, independent ADLs, driving, and lifting up to 25 lbs, clearing him for modified light/medium duty return to NSK.
